title: Solving the Cylinder Formula for Height
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A right circular cylinder has fixed volume $100$ cubic units. Write the height $h$ as a function of the base radius $r$, and note how $h$ behaves as $r$ grows.

steps.title: Start from the Volume Law
steps.explanation: Cylinder volume equals base area $\pi r^2$ times height $h$; set this product to the fixed value $100$.
steps.why: The constraint equation couples the two free dimensions.

steps.title: Isolate the Height
steps.explanation: Dividing both sides by $\pi r^{2}$ expresses $h$ purely in terms of $r$.
steps.why: Solving for one variable produces a genuine function of the other.

steps.title: Describe Domain and Behavior
steps.explanation: Radii must be positive. The inverse-square law means a slender cylinder is very tall and a squat one is nearly flat.
steps.why: Asymptotic behavior of a reciprocal-square model captures the thin-versus-wide trade-off.
steps.mathExpression: r>0,\quad h\to\infty \text{ as } r\to 0^{+},\quad h\to 0 \text{ as } r\to\infty
